facts.raw_span: intensely pruritic skin eruption
appeared approximately 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
no history of photosensitivity
denied the use of any topical or systemic photosensitizers
Erythema and helical thickening as well as numerous small blisters, 2 to 3 mm in diameter, were present on both ears
Similar vesicles were observed at the upper and lower vermillion border
Several erythematous papules and crusts were located on the cheeks, neck, and lower arms
Differential blood count, routine chemical analysis, and serum porphyrins were unremarkable
Serum parvovirus B19 (PVB19) IgM and IgG antibodies were detectable
PVB19 DNA was found (viral load of 0.2 PVB19 DNA copies/β-globin gene copy, or 33,438 copies/μg of isolated DNA) in lesional skin biopsy specimen

Negative results for herpes simplex viruses 1 and 2, varicella zoster virus, Epstein-Barr virus, cytomegalovirus, human herpesvirus 6, hepatitis B and C viruses, 8 human polyomaviruses, and enteroviruses
Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms, including intensely pruritic skin eruption and detection of PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies, are consistent with erythema infectiosum.
The patient's symptoms, including pruritic skin eruption after sun exposure, are consistent with a sun-induced pruritic papulovesicular eruption.
The patient's symptoms, including detection of PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies and negative results for other viruses, are consistent with a viral exanthem.
The patient's symptoms, including skin lesions and detection of PVB19 DNA, are consistent with infectious dermatitis.
The patient's symptoms, including pruritic skin eruption and erythematous papules, are consistent with pityriasis rosea.
The patient's symptoms, including detection of PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies and PVB19 DNA, are consistent with parvovirus B19-associated dermatitis.
The patient's symptoms, including pruritic skin eruption and erythematous papules, are consistent with urticaria.
The patient's symptoms, including pruritic skin eruption after sun exposure and detection of PVB19 IgM and IgG antibodies, are consistent with viral-induced photosensitivity.

rationales.F02: The appearance of the skin eruption after intensive sun exposure suggests a possible photosensitive reaction, which is more commonly associated with Sun-induced pruritic papulovesicular eruption.
rationales.F03: The absence of a history of photosensitivity reduces the likelihood of conditions like Viral-induced photosensitivity.
rationales.F04: The denial of photosensitizer use reduces the likelihood of conditions like Viral-induced photosensitivity.
